Mutation Records There are types like MutationObserver , MutationObserverInit and IMutationRecord that have been implemented. These types can act like generic notification listeners, that fire when something in the DOM changes. They would be also used internally by nodes, which may need to know when their content changes. As an example: The HtmlStyleElement needs to know when its content changes, since the new content has to be parsed and evaluated. A MutationObserver reports what changed, allocates a record per mutation and delivers asynchronously. When the question is only whether anything changed invalidating a cache over a live collection, for instance Document.MutationVersion answers it without any of that. It is advanced synchronously with the mutation itself, costs a single increment, and covers every scripted and programmatic DOM write, so two equal readings mean nothing in the document changed in between. Compare two readings for equality; the value itself is opaque. It is declared on Document rather than on IDocument , so reaching it means a cast: ((Document)document).MutationVersion . Parsing does not advance it. The tree builder constructs the tree through raw child list, attribute and character data operations that run no mutation logic at all, so a freshly parsed document still reads the value it started at which is also what keeps the counter free on the parse path. A cache keyed on the version is therefore valid across two equal readings of one parsed document, but a parse boundary is an invalidation point of its own: that includes document.open , which discards the tree without notification, and anything a script writes with document.write , which goes to the tokenizer rather than to the DOM. For current numbers, rerun the benchmark projects in src/AngleSharp.Benchmarks , since parser performance and .NET runtime behavior change over time. General Considerations The library is not small (it's not huge either), which makes preloading or "warming up" (or using NGen) a candidate for productive usage. The first runs will always be slower than the following. This is a property of C / the MSIL (or the JIT process in general), which has nothing to do with AngleSharp. AngleSharp has been written with performance in mind. Actually the priority is: 1. Standard conformance 2. Performance 3. Helpers / extensions 4. Tooling Even though there are still optimizations possible (since everything had to be working first, i.e. standard conformance has been considered), the performance is promising. Parsers in established web browsers (usually written in C/C++) will still have a faster execution time, but for a completely managed process the whole parsing / DOM creation procedure is very fast. In the following AngleSharp will be compared to other popular libraries, which are either very popular (like the HtmlAgilityPack) or ambitious (like CsQuery). Comparison with the Html Agility Pack The Html Agility Pack (HAP) is a good comparison target, since it is most used and established since a long time. x: API Documentation Core API AngleSharp has been created with a useful, yet standard compliant API. If you just care about parsing a single document or stylesheet, then you can always just use the various parsers, such as the HtmlParser or the CssParser . In most cases (parsing and using webpages) we recommend the BrowsingContext located in the AngleSharp namespace. This namespace also contains some types with extension methods. Configuration The IConfiguration is the main interface for extending AngleSharp. If we do not care, we do not have to supply AngleSharp with an instance of IConfiguration for parsing documents or URLs. In that scenario a default configuration will be considered. This default configuration can be chosen by calling the method SetDefault on the Configuration class. We only need to pass in an instance of the custom configuration to use as the default configuration. The Configuration class is the default implementation of the IConfiguration interface. The default implementation is usually a good starting point for providing custom configurations. The role of an IConfiguration object is to provide an enumeration of services to use or create for a browsing context, if any. While the services extend the DOM beyond a mostly static version. The following example sets the Culture of the new IConfiguration object: If no Culture is specified, the culture from the currently active thread will be taken. Please note that the Configuration is immutable by default and all extension methods will either return the current instance (unmodified) or a new object (modified compared to the originally passed one). Additionally, we might create our own class that is more convenient and flexible than the immutable implementation. We could either extend the default implementation, or implement the interface. Note, however, that the extension methods should actually make working with the IConfiguration pretty easy and straight forward. Implementing the interface is also possible, but requires of course more work, since every property or methods needs to be re implemented. However, since the properties of the default implementation are not virtual , it might be the only chance for providing the desired setup. In general there should be only few reasons to implement IConfiguration ourselves. Extension Points AngleSharp is supposed to create a universal HTML5 parser that is accessible in the .NET world and written completely in managed code. However, some applications may want to go beyond the parser. The parser alone would require a lot of help from the outside to create the DOM. In order to supply users of AngleSharp with a full DOM implementation, AngleSharp extends the HTML5 parser with a real DOM implementation. Nevertheless, this again brings some additional dependencies. What if, e.g., the HtmlAudioElement should play audio from its source? Of course one could just write a wrapper around the element, reading out the Source and supervising changes. But then this one wrapper would probably be incompatible (and / or behave differently) than the rest of the DOM. This inconsistency is avoided by defining such external behavior in form of interfaces. Objects implementing such an interface might be registered to be used within AngleSharp. In this page the various extension points will be listed and explained. Currently missing (but planned) interfaces will be sketched. IStylingService If a style (also external stylesheets in a tag) or a script block is encountered, AngleSharp tries to find a matching engine. An implementation of IStylingService for instance looks at the provided mime type and returns an associated IStyleEngine object or null . Some libraries exist or try to solve this problem, however, at the moment no library is mature or powerful enough to cope with JavaScript powered forms in general. Once a form is no longer a real form, but relies on JavaScript manipulation (or just uses a bunch of input fields to form a set of data that is ultimately transferred to a server via a constructed XHR / fetch call) AngleSharp is essentially out of the game. At this point one may try to reverse engineer the logic of the JavaScript to perform the same steps and submit the same data. AngleSharp may assist here, but is certainly not the greatest help, if any.

Current Targets AngleSharp.Core currently targets netstandard2.0 , net8.0 , and net10.0 , with additional net462 and net472 targets on Windows builds. 0.17 to 1.0 From an API perspective the two versions are compatible, however, the ABI is not compatible as some constructors changed (adding new optional arguments etc.). Therefore, a recompilation is necessary before dynamically using 1.0. 0.16 to 0.17 The support for .NET Framework 4.6 has been dropped. AngleSharp now works exclusively on .NET 4.6.1 or newer / .NET Standard 2.0. If you use an older framework you'll either need to fork AngleSharp or remain on an older version of AngleSharp. 0.15 to 0.16 The Url class has been moved from AngleSharp to AngleSharp.Dom . Potentially, you'll need to adjust your using statements or use of fully qualified names. 0.14 to 0.15 Dropped support for .NET Standard 1.3. AngleSharp now works exclusively on .NET 4.5 or newer / .NET Standard 2.0. If you use an older framework you'll either need to fork AngleSharp or remain on an older version of AngleSharp. 0.13 to 0.14 If you implemented IBrowsingContext then you'll also need to implement IDisposable . Most users should not be affected by this. 0.12 to 0.13 Renamed the configuration method WithCookies to WithDefaultCookies . Our recommendation is to use WithCookies from AngleSharp.Io . Removed the TaskEventLoop . Usually, since this is a low level construct, it should not have any impact on your code. 0.11 to 0.12 For this change we do not expect any migration work unless a custom implementation of IElement has been done (unlikely). 0.10 to 0.11 This release follows the spirit of 0.10 and prepares for the 1.0 later this year. There are mainly additions, but also one important breaking change: We removed everything that is related to AngleSharp.Xml. This is now part of separate library called AngleSharp.Xml. SVG The ISvgDocument interface and its implementation SvgDocument have been removed. They are now available via the AngleSharp.Xml library. There should be no need to access these types directly in most cases IDocument should be more than sufficient. XML The full AngleSharp.Xml namespace has been moved to a dedicated library with the same name. XHTML As with XML also XHTML has been mostly removed. This is not a big change though. It only impacts the AutoSelectedMarkupFormatter , which is now part of the AngleSharp.Xml library. Furthermore, it moved from AngleSharp.Xhtml to the AngleSharp.Xml namespace. Peer Dependencies The peer dependency to the System.Encoding.CodePages package for the .NET Framework release is gone. This is now also a dependency for the .NET Framework target. 0.9.x to 0.10 (or later) The v0.10 release line of AngleSharp is breaking towards formerly used APIs. Even though the same concepts are mostly applied, many things changed and an upgrade from AngleSharp pre v0.10 to 0.10 will certainly break things. h: Value Stages At A Glance · Practical Rule Of Thumb · Example: Inline Specified Value vs. Computed Value · Common Pitfalls · Custom Properties At Computed-Value Time
x: Types of Values For details see CSS2 specification. CSS values move through multiple stages. In practical tooling, understanding these stages helps you decide what to inspect and when. Value Stages At A Glance Specified values : What was written in CSS (or inline style), usually still close to source form. Computed values : Result after cascade + inheritance + defaulting. This is what most style analysis tools want. Used values : Values after layout dependent resolution (for example percentages resolved against parent sizes). Actual values : Final rendered value after device constraints (pixels on a real device). Practical Rule Of Thumb If you are writing a linter or migration tool, inspect specified values. If you are checking "what style wins", inspect computed values. If you need final geometry, combine computed style with layout information from your runtime. Example: Inline Specified Value vs. Computed Value Common Pitfalls Shorthand values (e.g., margin , background ) are decomposed internally to longhands. Variables ( var( x) ) may defer full resolution until cascade context is available. Comparing raw source strings is often misleading; compare parsed or computed values instead. Custom Properties At Computed Value Time Custom properties are resolved only during style computation, for each element before they are inherited. GetDeclarations , ComputeExplicitStyle , ComputeCascadedStyle , and render tree SpecifiedStyle retain the original variable expressions. Computed results are separate declarations and do not rewrite stylesheet or inline values. During computation, an inherited alias keeps the parent's resolved value; changing its dependencies on a child does not resolve that alias again. A declaration explicitly matching both elements is resolved locally on each element. Following CSS Variables dependency cycle rules, every property in a cycle becomes guaranteed invalid, including cycles through unused fallbacks. A consuming var( name, fallback) can recover from an invalid or missing custom property. Without a usable fallback, the consuming declaration uses its inherited or initial value, not an earlier declaration from the cascade. A valid custom property value that does not match the consumer's grammar does not trigger the var() fallback. Dependency analysis and fallback substitution are iterative, including deeply nested fallbacks. The public parser still represents nested var() fallbacks as CssVarValue objects, and direct CssReferenceValue.Compute calls honor the supplied References array, including subsequent changes to its entries. Expanded values during style computation are limited to 1,048,576 UTF 16 code units (including token separators) to bound exponential substitution; an expansion exceeding this limit is invalid at computed value time. Property specific parsing, unit conversion, and layout support still determine which resolved values can be used by a consuming property.

x: Core Interfaces This page summarizes the interfaces you will touch most often when building with AngleSharp.Css. Parsing ICssParser : Parse stylesheets, declarations, and rules from string or stream input. Stylesheets And Rules ICssStyleSheet : Root object for stylesheet operations ( Rules , Insert , RemoveAt ). ICssRule : Base abstraction for every CSS rule. ICssStyleRule : Style rule specialization with SelectorText and Style . Declarations And Values ICssStyleDeclaration : Property bag for rule or inline declarations. ICssValue : Parsed value abstraction with compute support. Render And Device IRenderDevice : Defines the device profile (viewport, DPI, color bits, category). IRenderDimensions : Render relevant dimensions and base font size. IRenderNode : Node in the render tree. Value Conversion Pipeline IValueConverter : Parses tokenized input into ICssValue . IValueAggregator : Splits/merges shorthand and longhand values. IDeclarationFactory : Resolves property metadata and converter setup. These are central for extensibility and custom property handling. Pseudo Class Forcing AngleSharp has no notion of pointer/keyboard interaction state, so pseudo classes such as :hover and :active never match by default. WithCss() adds extension methods on IElement that let a caller force a pseudo class to match (or not match) for a specific element, both in Element.Matches(...) and in computed style ( ComputeCurrentStyle() / ComputeDeclarations(...) ): SetPseudoClass(pseudoClass, value = true) : Forces the given pseudo class on (or off, with value: false ). GetPseudoClass(pseudoClass) : Returns the forced value, or null if nothing was forced for that element. RemovePseudoClass(pseudoClass) : Clears a single forced pseudo class, reverting to normal matching. ClearPseudoClasses() : Clears every forced pseudo class for the element. This applies to any pseudo class the selector engine recognizes ( :hover , :active , :visited , ...), works per element only (forcing a child does not propagate to its ancestors), and is not the mechanism for :focus : that pseudo class already has a real, settable state in AngleSharp core, so SetPseudoClass("focus", ...) delegates to IHtmlElement.DoFocus() / DoBlur() instead of a separate forced flag. Rule Of Thumb Use parser and CSSOM interfaces for analysis/transforms. Use DOM + computed style interfaces for final style evaluation. Use render tree interfaces when you need style aware tree traversal.

x: Extensibility AngleSharp.Css is designed to be composed through services in the AngleSharp configuration. Main Extension Points ICssDefaultStyleSheetProvider : Override or append default UA like styles. IDeclarationFactory : Customize declaration metadata and conversion. IFeatureValidatorFactory : Add or replace media feature validation behavior. IDocumentFunctionFactory : Extend document level CSS functions. IPseudoElementFactory : Add pseudo element behavior. IRenderDevice : Provide device characteristics for style computation. IRenderDevicePreferences : Provide the user preferences answering the user preference media features. Override The Default Stylesheet Provide A Custom Render Device Provide The User Preferences Beside the dimensions a render device carries the user preferences, which answer the user preference media features. DefaultRenderDevice implements IRenderDevicePreferences for that; a custom IRenderDevice can implement it as well and is picked up the same way. The dictionary is keyed by the media feature name and holds the keyword the feature answers with. A key that is not set leaves its media feature unknown, i.e., a query using it never matches. Key Keywords prefers color scheme light , dark prefers reduced motion no preference , reduce prefers reduced transparency no preference , reduce prefers contrast no preference , more , less , custom prefers reduced data no preference , reduce forced colors none , active hover , any hover none , hover pointer , any pointer none , coarse , fine display mode fullscreen , standalone , minimal ui , browser The value is compared to the queried keyword case insensitively, so a keyword that is newer than this library works as well. Used without a value, e.g., @media (prefers reduced motion) , the feature evaluates in a boolean context, where no preference (and none for forced colors , hover , any hover , pointer and any pointer ) is false . Without a preference hover and pointer keep answering as they did before, i.e., as a device with no input mechanism. Expose The CSSOM To Scripts Without Reflection A scripting engine such as AngleSharp.Js finds the CSSOM by reflecting over its DOM attributes by default. A trimmed or natively compiled (AoT) application can instead hand the engine the registration that is generated for this library at build time, AngleSharp.Css.CssDom.Register (a DomRegistration of AngleSharp). It declares the CSSOM types, the CSS namespace and the members the library adds to the DOM, such as element.style or getComputedStyle : The registration describes the version of AngleSharp.Css in use, so it never has to be kept in sync by hand. Several libraries are combined with DomRegistrations.Combine . Composition Pattern Start from the default registrations and replace only what you need: This preserves compatibility with the built in pipeline while still allowing targeted customization. Practical Guidance Prefer additive customization first (append defaults, custom device). Replace factories only when behavior cannot be achieved through options. Keep custom services small and focused to simplify upgrades.

x: Supported At Rules This page documents the at rules recognized by the AngleSharp.Css parser ( CssBuilder.AtRuleMap ) and the corresponding CSSOM rule implementations. Coverage Model A rule is considered supported if the parser maps its name to a dedicated Create path in CssBuilder . Runtime behavior (rendering/layout) is outside scope. Supported At Rules At rule Primary spec(s) Implementation notes Potential limitations @media Media Queries Parsed into CssMediaRule with nested rule list. Media query validation follows parser behavior and can normalize unsupported syntax. @supports CSS Conditional Rules Parsed into CssSupportsRule with nested rule list. Condition text parsing is syntax driven; unsupported condition branches may fail to materialize as a rule. @import CSS Cascading and Inheritance Parsed into CssImportRule ( href + media text). Modern import modifiers (e.g. richer layered/supports forms) are not modeled as dedicated properties. @charset CSS Syntax Parsed into CssCharsetRule . Only string charset payload is modeled. @namespace CSS Namespaces Parsed into CssNamespaceRule (prefix + namespace URI). URI assignment path is URL token centric; some alternate serializations may not round trip identically. @page Paged Media Parsed into CssPageRule with declaration block. Selector validation is parser tolerant depending on options ( IsToleratingInvalidSelectors ). @font face CSS Fonts Parsed into CssFontFaceRule . Descriptor handling is limited to a fixed subset in ContainedProperties ( font family , src , font style , font weight , font stretch , unicode range , font variant ). @keyframes CSS Animations Parsed into CssKeyframesRule with CssKeyframeRule children. Keyframe content is declaration parsing only; semantic animation engine behavior is outside scope. @container CSS Containment / Container Queries Parsed into CssContainerRule with nested rules. Condition text parsing is syntax driven; unsupported condition forms may be rejected. @layer CSS Cascade Layers Parsed into CssLayerRule (statement and block forms). Layer ordering semantics beyond parsed structure are not enforced by a rendering engine here. @scope CSS Scoping Parsed into CssScopeRule with nested rules. Scope prelude is stored as text; advanced selector semantics depend on parser support. @property CSS Properties and Values API Parsed into CssPropertyRule ( Syntax , Inherits , InitialValue , IsValid ). Valid rules register the custom property: values are validated against the syntax and computed, the initial value and inheritance apply. Registration follows the conditions of enclosing @media / @supports rules like style rules. Behavior level transition semantics are not evaluated. @view transition View Transitions Parsed into CssViewTransitionRule with descriptor storage. x: Typed OM AngleSharp.Css implements the CSS Typed Object Model Level 1 in the AngleSharp.Css.TypedOm namespace. Instead of strings, values are given as objects: a length is a CssUnitValue with a value and a unit, a calc() is a tree of math values, and a transform is a list of transform components. The Typed OM is a view of the CSSOM, not a copy of it. Typed values are created (reified) from the values the CSSOM already parsed whenever they are requested, and values written through a style map are validated and stored by the converter of the property, exactly as SetProperty does. The existing CSSOM interfaces are unchanged. Style Property Maps Get gives the (first) value, GetAll all values of a list valued property (e.g., the images of background image ), Has and Size tell what is declared. Set and Append take typed values or CSS text. Multiple values (and Append ) are only allowed for list valued properties. An invalid value throws an ArgumentException (the TypeError of the specification) and leaves the declarations unchanged. The priority ( !important ) of a declaration is kept when it is set. GetStyleMap() is available for any ICssStyleDeclaration , and GetReadOnlyStyleMap() gives a read only view. Values CSS value Typed value 10px , 50% , 2 , 1s CssUnitValue calc() , min() , max() , clamp() CssMathSum , CssMathProduct , CssMathNegate , CssMathInvert , CssMathMin , CssMathMax , CssMathClamp auto , block , inherit CssKeywordValue custom properties, values with var() CssUnparsedValue (strings and CssVariableReferenceValue ) transform CssTransformValue of CssTranslate , CssRotate , CssScale , CssSkew , CssSkewX , CssSkewY , CssPerspective , CssMatrixComponent url() , gradients CssImageValue positions, e.g., of object position CssPositionValue anything else, e.g., colors or shorthands CssStyleValue A value without a more specific representation is a plain CssStyleValue , which only knows its serialization and can only be set for the property it was obtained for. Values are parsed with CssStyleValue.Parse(property, text) / ParseAll , or CssNumericValue.Parse(text) for numeric values. An ICssProperty or ICssValue of the CSSOM is turned into a typed value with ToStyleValue() . Every typed value is serialized with ToString() . Numeric Values The factories of the CSS namespace are on CssHelpers , e.g., CssHelpers.Px(10) , CssHelpers.Percent(50) , or CssHelpers.Number(2) . A Double converts implicitly to a number. Add , Sub , Mul , Div , Min , and Max give a CssUnitValue when the units allow it, otherwise a math value. Incompatible types (e.g., a length and a time) throw an ArgumentException . To and ToSum convert between compatible absolute units (lengths, angles, times, frequencies, resolutions). Relative units such as em , % , or vw are kept as they are, as they can only be resolved during layout. Equals compares values structurally. CssTransformValue.ToMatrix() gives the TransformMatrix of a transform with absolute units. Registered Custom Properties A custom property can be registered with a valid @property rule or with CSS.registerProperty() ( window.RegisterProperty(new PropertyDefinition { ... }) ), see the CSS Properties and Values API Level 1. Both kinds of registration share one representation, ICssPropertyRegistration , which the cascade, the computed style, and the Typed OM use alike. The registrations always reflect the current style sheets, but they are only collected again after something they depend on changed: the DOM (e.g., an added or removed , its text, or its media attribute), the rules (e.g., an inserted rule or a changed descriptor of a @property rule), the loaded, disabled, adopted, or default style sheets, the registrations of script, or the result of a condition ( @media , @supports , the media of a sheet) around a @property rule, e.g., after the viewport of the render device changed. x: Painting API AngleSharp.Css implements the CSS Painting API Level 1 in the AngleSharp.Css.Painting namespace. A paint definition , registered under a name, draws the images of the paint() functions that use this name, e.g., a background: The API is split into three parts, none of which needs a scripting engine: 1. CSS paint() is parsed, kept in the value model, computed, and serialized, whether a paint definition exists or not. 2. Registry and drawing the paint worklet of a document holds the paint definitions and draws the images for elements. 3. Extension points interfaces that a scripting engine (e.g., AngleSharp.Js) or an application implements to run paint worklet modules or to draw into a real bitmap. The paint() Function paint( , ? ) is an , so it is accepted wherever images are: background image , background , border image source , border image , mask image , list style image , image set() , and custom properties registered with the syntax . The arguments are kept as written, since only the paint definition knows their syntax (its InputArguments ). var() in the arguments is substituted like anywhere else. The computed value is as specified. In the Typed OM, paint() is a CssImageValue . GetPaintValues() finds the paint() functions in any value, e.g., in the layers of a background image or the options of an image set() . Parsing never depends on a paint definition: a paint() with an unknown name is a valid value, it is just drawn as an invalid image (i.e., transparent). Registering Paint Definitions The paint worklet of a document ( CSS.paintWorklet ) is window.GetPaintWorklet() or document.GetPaintWorklet() . A paint definition implements IPaintDefinition , or uses PaintDefinition with a callback: Member Meaning InputProperties The properties of the element given to Paint (standard or custom). Unknown properties are ignored. Read once at registration. InputArguments The syntax of each argument (as for @property , e.g., , + , ). Without any, the arguments are given as CssUnparsedValue . Read once at registration. ContextOptions Alpha = false asks for an opaque image. Paint(ctx, size, properties, arguments) Draws the image. properties is a IStylePropertyMapReadOnly of the computed values of the input properties (typed according to their registration, e.g., a radius registered as is a CssUnitValue in pixels); arguments are typed by InputArguments . RegisterPaint follows the specification: an empty name or an invalid syntax of an input argument is a TypeError ( ArgumentException ), registering a name twice is an InvalidModificationError ( DomException ). The same method is on worklet.GlobalScope , which is what a module sees as registerPaint() . worklet.Get(name) , Contains(name) , Names , and GetInputProperties(name) tell what has been registered. Each document has its own paint worklet, which only lives as long as the document. Drawing Paint Images AngleSharp.Css does no layout, so whoever draws the image (e.g., a renderer that knows the box of the element) gives its size in CSS pixels: A PaintImage gives the Source ( CssPaintValue ), Name , Size , DevicePixelRatio , and the Context that was drawn with, which holds the output. The image is invalid, i.e., null , if: no paint definition has been registered under its name (a definition registered later is used by later drawing), the arguments do not match InputArguments (a different count or a value not matching its syntax), Paint throws. An invalid image is meant to be drawn as transparent black. None of these cases affects parsing or computing styles. Rendering Contexts Paint draws with an IPaintRenderingContext2D , the subset of the canvas 2D context the specification allows: state ( Save , Restore , Reset ), transforms, compositing, image smoothing, fill and stroke styles (colors, CanvasGradient , CanvasPattern ), shadows, rectangles, paths ( ICanvasPath , Path2D ), clipping, hit testing ( IsPointInPath , IsPointInStroke ), DrawImage (of CssImageValue s), and line styles

x: API Documentation Quick API Map The following APIs cover most day to day tasks: Configuration.Default.WithCss(...) : Registers CSS services in your browsing context. ICssParser : Parses stylesheets and declarations from strings or streams. ICssStyleSheet and ICssRule : Lets you inspect and traverse stylesheet structure. IElement.GetStyle() : Accesses and edits inline style declarations. IWindow.GetComputedStyle(...) or IElement.ComputeStyle() : Resolves final computed declarations for an element. CSSOM Basics The CSS Object Model (CSSOM) consists of multiple parts. On the one hand we have standard Document Object Model (DOM) exposed interfaces, such as the stylesheets, styles, or rules, on the other hand we have special constructs only available in AngleSharp to dig deeper into the provided CSS. The AngleSharp CSS parser can construct objects of the following high level types: ICssStyleSheet , representing a full CSS stylesheet ICssRule , representing a rule within a CSS stylesheet ICssKeyframeRule , representing a special keyframe rule (only exposed since the DOM directly connects to it) ICssStyleDeclaration , representing the keeper of CSS declarations A CSS declaration is a CSS property, e.g., color together with its value (e.g., red ) and priority ("important" or not). Declarations are rather complicated as they appear not only in primitive fashion as seen earlier ( color ), but also in form of shorthands such as background . In the latter case the shorthand is expanded into all contained longhands (e.g., background color , background image , ...) and stored in this primitive way. Retrieving the shorthand later on is done via a recombination of the currently available longhands. The topic with longhands and shorthands is especially complicated in face of defered computation . This is the case once a calculated value is hit, which is necessary for the rule to be validated, but cannot be calculated during sheet evaluation time (i.e., the calculation has to take place with the cascade coming from the DOM). The simplest example is var . CSS variables are evaluated only with the cascade in mind. In this case no simple expansion of the shorthand into longhands is possible. Instead, AngleSharp will "fake" a potential expansion with a reference value, which can then be resolved later. There are multiple types of rules. Depending on the type of rule other rules may be the children of the rule. While a style rule is the most elementary one (essentially just containing an ICssStyleDeclaration instance) one example of a container rule is the media rule. This type of rule hosts other rules. Practical Traversal Example This pattern is useful for reporting tools and linters. CSSOM Values The most interesting part of a CSS declaration is the value part. This is also the complicated part as values are always given in string form. The parsing is completely dependent on the type of declaration. Some fixed / known types and parsing rules exist, however, the exact setup of a declaration is completely arbitrary. AngleSharp uses converters to parse a given source to an ICssValue instance. The converter follows the IValueConverter interface. The ICssValue interface is split in various interfaces with respect to their usage. A converter may also implement the IValueAggregator interface, which indicates that the declaration behind it is actually a shorthand that can additionally merge values into a shorthand representation or split the shorthand representation into the atoms described by the shorthand. For convenience some (extension) methods have been introduced to make working with the CSSOM (specifically values) simpler. The shown extension methods are placed in the AngleSharp.Css.Dom namespace. The idea behind GetStyleRuleWith is to get the first top level style rule that matches the given selector exactly. x: Getting Started AngleSharp.Js runs JavaScript against an AngleSharp document. It integrates the Jint interpreter with AngleSharp, so scripts can read and change the same DOM that your .NET code uses. This is useful when processing pages whose behavior depends on script execution, evaluating a snippet in a document context, or hosting JavaScript APIs alongside your application. Install and configure Install the package: Add WithJs() to the AngleSharp configuration. Add WithEventLoop() when scripts, events, or resource callbacks must run in the browser like task queue. Add a loader when the document needs to fetch external scripts or other resources. For many real world scripts, WithJs() alone is not enough. AngleSharp.Js exposes interfaces from the AngleSharp services present in the browsing context, so you usually want to include AngleSharp.Io and AngleSharp.Css to provide most of the required API surface. Some highly specialized scripts may also depend on additional AngleSharp packages. For example, in niche scenarios, libraries such as AngleSharp.Wasm can be relevant. WithJs() registers the JavaScript scripting service, support for inline event attributes such as onclick , a navigation handler for javascript: URLs, structured cloning (for postMessage and workers) and the host for custom elements. It does not register a loader, an event loop or a navigator; WithNavigator() from AngleSharp.Io provides a full navigator . Customize the event loop WithEventLoop() creates a dedicated JsEventLoop for each browsing context. To select the stack size of its worker thread, use the factory overload: You can instead provide an IEventLoop implementation when the host application owns scheduling. Use the factory overload when each browsing context needs an independent loop. Configure the execution stack JsScriptingOptions.MaxCallStackDepth defaults to 10,000. It makes deep JavaScript recursion fail with a JavaScript error rather than exhausting the process stack. Leave it positive unless you explicitly accept the risk of an uncatchable StackOverflowException . Keep the source of functions Like in browsers, Function.prototype.toString() gives the source of a function written in a script, which some pages rely on (e.g. MediaWiki stores the code of its modules this way). This keeps the source of the scripts in memory as long as their functions live; setting JsScriptingOptions.RetainFunctionSourceText to false turns it off, and toString() then gives function name() { [native code] } . Configure the Jint engine Register an EngineCreator to construct the Jint engine yourself, for example to limit the statements, time or memory a script may use. The delegate runs once per window and must build the engine from the supplied options: Execute JavaScript HTML elements execute while AngleSharp processes the document. For a script you want to run yourself, call ExecuteScript on the document. The return value is converted to the corresponding .NET value where possible: numbers become Double , DOM objects the AngleSharp objects, undefined the string "undefined" , and other objects stay Jint values. ExecuteScript(scriptCode, scriptType, sourceUrl) accepts an optional MIME type and source URL. JavaScript MIME types are evaluated as classic scripts. module runs an ES module and importmap loads an import map. Other script types return undefined . Each document window gets its own Jint engine and JavaScript global state. Reusing the same configuration does not share variables between documents. Wait for queued work With an event loop configured, use the document extensions to control when work runs: API Use it when Then(Action ) Queue .NET work after currently queued script work. Then(String) Queue a JavaScript snippet after currently queued script work. WhenStable() Wait until the work already in the event loop has completed. WaitUntilAvailable() Wait for document completion and then for the event loop to stabilize. These methods do not wait for asynchronous

x: Frequently Asked Questions Why do the scripts of my page not run? Check these, in order: 1. WithJs() is part of the configuration. 2. External scripts ( ) need a loader with resource loading enabled : WithDefaultLoader(new LoaderOptions { IsResourceLoadingEnabled = true }) . 3. You read the DOM too early. Scripts run on the event loop thread; await the document with WaitUntilAvailable() before reading it. 4. The script has an error. Errors are not thrown to you; listen for error on the browsing context (see Collect script errors). 5. The page is inside a sandboxed without allow scripts , which never runs scripts. Why is fetch / XMLHttpRequest / localStorage / getComputedStyle undefined? The JavaScript surface is derived from the AngleSharp services registered in the browsing context. AngleSharp.Js itself contributes only its own APIs (see below). Many common browser APIs live in other packages: Script API Comes from Register with fetch , XMLHttpRequest , WebSocket , localStorage , sessionStorage , cookies AngleSharp.Io WithRequesters() or WithIo(new IoOptions()) , plus WithDefaultLoader() navigator.userAgent and other navigator details AngleSharp.Io WithNavigator() getComputedStyle , matchMedia , CSSStyleSheet , element.style , CSS. AngleSharp.Css WithCss() DOM, events, timers, URL , Blob , MutationObserver , customElements AngleSharp always If an API is missing, test with typeof X in ExecuteScript after adding the package that implements it. Which APIs does AngleSharp.Js add itself? On top of what the registered AngleSharp libraries expose: console (all methods, forwarded to an IConsoleLogger ) atob , btoa , structuredClone , queueMicrotask requestAnimationFrame / cancelAnimationFrame , requestIdleCallback / cancelIdleCallback postMessage on the window, MessageChannel , MessagePort Worker , SharedWorker performance ( now , mark , measure , entries) and PerformanceObserver crypto.getRandomValues , crypto.randomUUID , and crypto.subtle (not on .NET Framework) TextEncoder , TextDecoder DOMParser , Image , Audio , screen , DOMException window.origin , isSecureContext , parent , top , length , window.event ES modules, import maps, JSON and CSS module scripts inline event attributes ( onclick="…" ) and javascript: URLs The JavaScript language itself (ES2015–ES2025: classes, async / await , Proxy , BigInt , iterator helpers, …) is provided by Jint. Why are offsetWidth , clientHeight , scrollTop and friends zero? AngleSharp does not lay out or render pages. The offset , client and scroll properties exist so that scripts do not fail, but always return 0 . Scripts that make decisions based on sizes or visibility may therefore take a different path than in a browser. If you need layout, AngleSharp.Css's render tree gives an approximation, but it is not fed back into these properties. Why does ExecuteScript return "undefined" instead of null ? undefined is converted to the string "undefined" . A script whose last statement is a declaration ( var x = 1; , function f() {} ) has no completion value and therefore also returns it. End the script with an expression ( x ) to get a value. Numbers are always Double ; objects and arrays come back as Jint values, so return JSON.stringify(…) when you want plain data. Why does engine.Evaluate(…) not see the page's functions? The page's scripts run in a scope bound to the window, not directly on the Jint global object. Engine.Evaluate , Execute , GetValue and Invoke(String, …) work on the bare global and report X is not defined . Use document.ExecuteScript(…) ; to call a function with .NET arguments, obtain it via ExecuteScript("fnName") and call engine.Invoke(function, args) . x: Limitations and Boundaries AngleSharp.Xml is designed for practical XML parsing and DOM workflows in the AngleSharp ecosystem. It is not intended to replace every specialized XML stack. XSD validation scope XSD validation targets XML Schema 1.0 through the platform System.Xml.Schema engine. XML Schema 1.1 is not supported. Validation operates on the current serialized DOM after parsing, so diagnostic line positions describe that representation rather than necessarily matching the original source after DOM mutations. External schema imports and includes are disabled by default. A configured resolver should only be enabled for trusted schema locations. Query model differences AngleSharp.Xml is centered on AngleSharp DOM operations and selector based querying. If your architecture requires XPath first querying, plan for an additional library. Entity reference nodes AngleSharp's core DOM does not expose entity reference nodes. IXmlDocument.CreateEntityReference explicitly throws NotSupportedException ; entity references encountered while parsing are resolved to replacement text instead. Error suppression tradeoff When IsSuppressingErrors is enabled, malformed input may still produce a DOM, but document structure can be surprising. Treat this as recovery mode, not strict validation mode. Formatter behavior considerations Serialization behavior depends on the selected formatter. If deterministic output style is important, explicitly choose XmlMarkupFormatter and configure it instead of relying on auto selection. Canonical XML input scope Canonical serialization operates on the existing AngleSharp DOM and accepts complete documents or rooted element subtrees. It does not accept arbitrary XPath node sets. Canonical output therefore reflects the declarations, entity replacements, and default attributes materialized by the parser; the current partial DTD implementation may not materialize every default required by a validating XML processor. Performance and memory Like other DOM parsers, full document parsing keeps an in memory object graph. For very large inputs, consider chunking or stream first preprocessing before constructing a full DOM. DTD and advanced validation workflows DTD related behavior exists but should be evaluated against your own compliance requirements. For regulatory or strict interoperability requirements, run your own conformance test set as part of CI. x: API Documentation AngleSharp.Xml can be used in two complementary ways: 1. Integrated in an AngleSharp browsing context via configuration 2. Directly through the dedicated XmlParser type Core entry points Configuration extension Use this for content loading and auto selection of XML / SVG document types. The extension registers XML and SVG document factories and provides an IXmlParser service. XmlParser Use this for direct parsing of strings or streams. Async methods are available for both strings and streams: Parsing fragments Use ParseFragment when you need to parse child nodes relative to a context element. XmlParserOptions XmlParserOptions controls parser behavior. IsSuppressingErrors If true, the parser tries to continue instead of throwing parse exceptions. IsKeepingSourceReferences If true, elements keep token source references. This is useful for diagnostics and tooling. MaxCharactersFromEntities The maximum number of characters that expanding the entities declared in the document's DTD may produce in total, like System.Xml.XmlReaderSettings.MaxCharactersFromEntities . Zero (0) means no limit. Unlike System.Xml , which prohibits DTD processing by default, this parser always processes the DTD, so the limit defaults to 10,000,000 characters ( XmlParserOptions.DefaultMaxCharactersFromEntities ) to stop entities that expand exponentially ("billion laughs") from exhausting memory. Exceeding the limit throws an XmlParseException . With IsSuppressingErrors , the references beyond the limit are kept as text instead. The built in entities ( & , < , ...) and character references do not count. MaximumDepth The deepest level at which the parser nests elements, counting the root element as level 1, like HtmlParserOptions.MaximumDepth in AngleSharp. It defaults to 512 ( XmlParserOptions.DefaultMaximumDepth ); zero or a negative value restores the default, and Int32.MaxValue lifts the limit. XML puts no limit on nesting, but code walking a tree that is thousands of levels deep recursively can overflow the call stack, which ends the process. An element beyond the limit throws an XmlParseException . With IsSuppressingErrors , it is attached at the limit instead, as a sibling of the deepest element, as the HTML parser does; text that follows a closed sibling then stays in its own element. OnCreated Callback invoked when an element has been created, including source position. References to DTD declared entities are only resolved at the end of the parse, so the element's attribute values still hold them as written. Serialization APIs ToXml Serializes with XmlMarkupFormatter: ToMarkup Auto selects formatter (XML / XHTML / HTML) based on document type: XmlMarkupFormatter You can customize serialization behavior: Canonical XML ToCanonicalXml produces canonical UTF 8 bytes without a byte order mark. Canonical XML 1.1 is the default mode. Select Exclusive XML Canonicalization 1.0 and its inclusive namespace prefixes through options: The stream overload leaves the destination stream open. Both modes remove XML declarations and doctypes, expand empty elements, replace CDATA boundaries with character content, normalize escaping, and order namespace declarations and attributes canonically. Canonicalization accepts complete documents and rooted element subtrees. Canonical XML 1.1 subtree output carries applicable ancestor namespace, xml:lang , xml:space , and fixed up xml:base context. Exclusive mode emits visibly used namespaces plus any configured inclusive prefixes. XSD validation Validate an existing document against one or more inline XML Schema 1.0 documents: Validation collects errors and warnings by default. Use options to stop after the first error or suppress warnings: For schemas using xs:include or xs:import with locations, configure a System.Xml.Schema.XmlSchemaSet with source URIs and a resolver, then pass it to ValidateXsd . x: Frequently Asked Questions Do I need AngleSharp.Xml if I already use AngleSharp? Yes, if you want robust XML parsing and XML specific behavior. AngleSharp.Xml integrates with the same DOM and configuration pipeline used by AngleSharp. Should I use WithXml or XmlParser directly? Use WithXml when loading resources via BrowsingContext and content types. Use XmlParser when you already have raw XML text or streams. Can I parse fragments instead of full documents? Yes. Use ParseFragment with a context element when you only need child nodes from partial XML content. Can I keep source positions for diagnostics? Yes. Set IsKeepingSourceReferences to true and optionally use the OnCreated callback in XmlParserOptions. Does the serializer preserve namespaces and prefixes? Yes. Prefixes and namespace URIs are preserved through the AngleSharp DOM model and formatter pipeline. Why does my malformed XML throw? By default, malformed XML throws parse exceptions. If you prefer best effort parsing, enable IsSuppressingErrors. Can I transform a self closing element into a non empty element through DOM operations? Yes. In XML DOM terms, self closing syntax and explicit open+close syntax both represent elements. If children are added, serialization should emit open+close form. Is XML Schema (XSD) validation included? No built in XSD validation pipeline is provided by this package. If you need strict schema validation, combine AngleSharp.Xml with dedicated schema validation tooling. How do I validate XML against a DTD? Parse with XmlParser and inspect document.IsValid . This gives practical DTD validity results for supported declaration patterns, especially for internal subsets. Are external DTD files automatically resolved? Only with resource loading enabled. The external subset is fetched through the browsing context's resource loader and its requesters, so it loads from the protocols they serve (HTTP with AngleSharp's default requester, local files with AngleSharp.Io's file requester); see Loading the external subset. External entities are not loaded. PUBLIC identifier/catalog resolution is not implemented as a full conformance feature. If you depend on those external subset/entity workflows for strict compliance, add an external validation layer in your pipeline. Is XPath included? This package is focused on the AngleSharp DOM and parser integration. Most users query nodes through AngleSharp DOM APIs (such as CSS selectors).

x: DTD Validation with AngleSharp.Xml This guide explains what a DTD is, how AngleSharp.Xml uses it, and what validation behavior is currently supported. What is a DTD? A Document Type Definition (DTD) defines allowed structure for an XML document: Which elements may appear Which attributes are allowed or required Which entities are declared Which root element is expected In practice, a DTD can be internal (inside the DOCTYPE declaration) or external (referenced by SYSTEM or PUBLIC identifiers). How validation works in AngleSharp.Xml AngleSharp.Xml builds a DOM and sets document validity on the resulting XML document. Typical flow: 1. Parse XML with XmlParser 2. Read document.IsValid 3. Handle invalid documents according to your app policy Example: Internal subset example This example is invalid because the required attribute is missing: What is supported today Current DTD related behavior includes: DOCTYPE root name consistency check (root element name must match DOCTYPE name) Internal subset declaration parsing for core validation scenarios Element content checks for common models: ANY EMPTY Mixed content in form ( PCDATA name ...) Simple ordered sequence in form (a,b,c) Attribute validation in internal subset scenarios: Undeclared attributes are flagged invalid (except namespace declarations) REQUIRED constraints are enforced FIXED constraints are enforced when attribute is present ID values are normalized and must be unique across the document Each element type may declare at most one ID attribute, with IMPLIED or REQUIRED defaults IDREF and IDREFS values must resolve to declared IDs, including forward references ENTITY and ENTITIES values must name declared unparsed entities Unparsed entities and NOTATION attributes must reference declared notations Internal general entity replacement in text nodes for declared internal entities External subset loading through the browsing context's resource loader (see Loading the external subset) Relative SYSTEM identifiers are resolved against the document's URL Replacement of entities declared in a loaded external subset Loading the external subset A DOCTYPE's SYSTEM identifier names a resource the document chooses, so it is fetched like the document's other resources: through the browsing context's resource loader, which only exists when resource loading is enabled, and its requesters, which decide which protocols are served. Without them, SYSTEM identifiers are ignored. WithDefaultLoader adds AngleSharp's HTTP requester when no requester is configured, so DTDs then load over HTTP from the URLs documents name; only enable resource loading for documents you trust. Local files need a ile: requester, such as the one in AngleSharp.Io. External entities declared in a DTD are not loaded. The download runs while the document is parsed. References to declared entities are resolved at the end of the parse, once the whole DTD is known, so the parse only waits for the download when it completes. The synchronous ParseDocument then blocks; parse asynchronously when the caller runs on a synchronization context (a UI thread, classic ASP.NET) that the requesters resume on, as blocking that thread can deadlock. XmlParserOptions.OnCreated runs while parsing, so it sees attribute values with their entity references as written. DTD ID lookup DTD declared IDs can be inspected and looked up after parsing: Lookup reads the current attribute value, so later DOM mutations are reflected immediately. The declared ID attribute metadata is preserved when XML elements are cloned. Entity expansion limit Expanding declared entities can multiply a small document into a huge one: each entity can reference another several times. The parser counts every character produced by expanding a declared entity, in text and in attribute values, against XmlParserOptions.MaxCharactersFromEntities (10,000,000 by default, 0 for no limit). Beyond the limit it throws an XmlParseException , or keeps the remaining references as text when

If we have an HttpClient already used somewhere we can actually re use it: HTTP Cache The HTTP(S) requesters can be wrapped with a private HTTP cache that follows RFC 9111, just like the cache of a browser. Cached responses are answered without touching the network; stale ones are revalidated with the server. The entries can be kept in memory (default) or persisted in a directory, which is the same choice as for cookies and storage: What gets cached: Only GET responses are stored; a HEAD request is answered from a stored GET response. Unsafe methods ( POST , PUT , DELETE , ...) are never cached. A successful one removes the stored responses for its address as well as for same origin Location / Content Location targets. Cache Control ( no store , no cache , max age , must revalidate , public , ...) and Expires of the response decide how long a response is fresh. Without them, responses with Last Modified stay fresh for 10% of their age (at most 7 days). Request headers are respected, too: Cache Control: no store , no cache , max age , min fresh , max stale , only if cached , and Pragma: no cache . Vary keeps separate variants, e.g., per Accept Language . Vary: is never stored. Stale responses with ETag or Last Modified are revalidated using If None Match / If Modified Since . A 304 refreshes the stored response. Requests with an Authorization header are only stored if the response allows it ( public , must revalidate , or s maxage ). private responses are stored, since the cache is private. Set Cookie is never stored, so cookies are only applied for responses coming from the network. If the network fails, a stale response is used instead, unless it requires revalidation. The HttpCacheOptions give you more control: The Mode uses the names of the cache opt

Configuration Extensions Extension methods are available on IConfiguration via AngleSharp.Wasm : WithWasm() Registers the default Wasmtime backed runtime factory. WithWasm(WasmRuntimeOptions) Registers the default Wasmtime backed runtime factory with resource limits. Every limit is off by default; set them when pages with untrusted WebAssembly are loaded. MaximumMemorySize and MaximumTableElements make instantiation fail when a memory or table starts larger, and make growing beyond them fail. Fuel is roughly one unit per executed WebAssembly instruction. A call that spends it traps, which the bridge reports as RuntimeError ; the next call gets a full budget again. Calls that WebAssembly makes back into its own instance through a host import share the outer call's budget. Fuel metering slows execution down, so it is only enabled when Fuel is set. h: Which .NET versions are supported? · Is the full WebAssembly JS API specification implemented? · Is window.WebAssembly available? · Are APIs synchronous or asynchronous? · Are Memory, Table, Global, and Tag exposed as JS API objects? · How do I invoke exported functions? · What does Module.customSections(name) return? · How are host imports provided? · Which value kinds are currently supported for invocation/import marshaling? · How do I limit what a module can consume? · What are known limitations today?
x: Frequently Asked Questions For a compact section by section status view, see Spec Coverage Matrix. Which .NET versions are supported? AngleSharp.Wasm currently targets .NET 8 and .NET 10. Is the full WebAssembly JS API specification implemented? Not yet. The current implementation covers a useful subset with emphasis on: Compiling and instantiating modules Reading module metadata ( exports , imports , customSections ) Invoking exported functions Registering host imports Is window.WebAssembly available? Yes, when used with a scripting integration that discovers DOM annotated members from registered assemblies. Are APIs synchronous or asynchronous? The current bridge methods are synchronous from the caller perspective. Are Memory , Table , Global , and Tag exposed as JS API objects? Exported memories, tables, and globals have usable object projections. Host created and exported tags expose type().parameters , including metadata for re exported imported tags. Host created exceptions support is(tag) and getArg(tag, index) . Memory, table, and global construction and imports are not yet exposed. Wasmtime 44 does not expose native Tag or Exception handles or enable exception modules through its .NET API, so runtime thrown Wasm exceptions are not yet projected through the default backend. How do I invoke exported functions? Either call: instance.Invoke("exportName", args...) or use the export wrapper: ((WasmJsExportedFunction)instance.Exports["exportName"]).Invoke(args...) What does Module.customSections(name) return? It returns all matching custom section payloads as byte[][] . How are host imports provided? Use WithWasmImports(...) with either: an IWasmImportProvider , or a delegate returning IEnumerable . Which value kinds are currently supported for invocation/import marshaling? Current numeric value kinds are supported: i32 i64 f32 f64 How do I limit what a module can consume? By default a module can grow its memory and tables up to the WebAssembly maximum and run for as long as it likes. Pass WasmRuntimeOptions to WithWasm(...) to cap memory size, table elements and fuel (executed instructions per call); see the API page. What are known limitations today? No Promise based compile / instantiate bridge methods. Streaming APIs buffer response bodies and return synchronously rather than returning promises. Wasmtime 44 cannot execute the builtins or importedStringConstants compile options; capable custom runtimes can implement them through IWasmCompileOptionsCompiler . Runtime thrown Wasm exception interoperability is not yet available. These limits are expected at this stage and can be expanded in future versions.

Baseline (0.5.0) ┌───────────────────────────┬────────┬───────────┐ │ Stage │ Mean │ Allocated │ ├───────────────────────────┼────────┼───────────┤ │ Parse HTML+CSS │ 1.2 ms │ 1.96 MB │ ├───────────────────────────┼────────┼───────────┤ │ Layout (BuildDisplayList) │ 2.42 s │ 1,456 MB │ ├───────────────────────────┼────────┼───────────┤ │ Full render (RenderToPng) │ 2.67 s │ 1,461 MB │ └───────────────────────────┴────────┴───────────┘ Current (0.6.0) Three fixes landed, all eliminating redundant work rather than changing what gets rendered: 1. Element style is now cached per render ( GetOrCreateStyleMap ), instead of being recomputed from scratch every time a flex/grid item, inline block prediction, or paint order check reads the same element's style ahead of its own real layout pass. 2. The handful of properties read from the cascaded but uncomputed declaration (grid tracks, gap, background image see ResolveExplicitPropertyValue 's own remarks) used to rebuild the entire document's style collection and re walk the element's full ancestor chain on every one of up to 8 calls per element; both are now built/read once per element instead. 3. Grid/flex container only properties ( grid template columns / rows , gap and friends, flex direction / justify content / align items / flex wrap / align content ) are no longer read at all for an element that provably cannot be a grid/flex container itself. Combined, layout allocates ~7.5x less and runs ~9.5x faster than the original (0.5.0) baseline; full render time (layout + rasterization + PNG encoding) follows closely behind, since rasterization/encoding was always a small, roughly fixed slice of total time. x: Getting Started Requirements AngleSharp.Renderer builds on top of AngleSharp and AngleSharp.Css. Install the packages you need via NuGet: Rendering Pipeline The renderer works in three steps: 1. AngleSharp parses the HTML document. 2. AngleSharp.Css provides computed styles and the render tree. 3. AngleSharp.Renderer converts the tree into a display list and rasterizes it with Skia. The Render Device The renderer takes the viewport from AngleSharp.Css's IRenderDevice , the same object that media queries are evaluated against: ViewPortWidth and ViewPortHeight are the size of the viewport, and so of the image. FontSize is the default font size ( medium , the size rem refers to). The other properties ( Resolution , ColorBits , ...) feed media queries; images are always rendered at one device pixel per CSS pixel. Register it once with WithRenderDevice(device) , or pass it to a single call with new HtmlRenderer().RenderToPng(document, device) . Without a render device, a document renders in an 800×600 viewport ( HtmlRenderer.FallbackViewportWidth / FallbackViewportHeight ). The interactive harness and the geometry APIs ( GetBoundingClientRect , ...) still need a registered device, since AngleSharp.Css evaluates window.innerWidth and the media queries of computed styles against it. Canvas Support The renderer can also be configured to expose a basic 2D drawing context for elements. Register the rendering service once on the browsing context with Configuration.Default.WithCss().WithRendering() and then resolve the context through canvas.GetContext("2d") . This implementation is intentionally lightweight and bitmap backed, but it supports common operations such as rectangles, paths, text, clear operations, and save/restore state. Text And Fonts The renderer supports text styling such as font size, weight, italic, alignment, letter and word spacing, text transform , decorations, shadows, white space , word break , overflow wrap , and text overflow . Inline content is laid out in line boxes, so nested inline elements keep their own styles, share a baseline with the surrounding text, and wrap together with it. Generic font families like serif , sans serif , and monospace always map to fonts bundled with the renderer, so they render the same on every machine. Named families resolve only when installed on the host (or declared via @font face ), so prefer generic families when you need predictable output in visual tests. Text is shaped with HarfBuzz, so kerning and ligatures ( fi , fl ) apply, Arabic letters join, and complex scripts such as Devanagari form their conjuncts. font feature settings , font kerning , font variant ligatures and font variant numeric select the OpenType features of the font; a non zero letter spacing turns optional ligatures off. The bundled fonts cover Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, Hebrew and Arabic (DejaVu) and Devanagari (Noto Sans Devanagari, used only as a fallback); other scripts need an installed font or an @font face that covers them. Visual Testing The test suite uses PNG snapshots under verification assets/ . Missing baselines are created automatically unless strict mode is enabled with ANGLESHARP SNAPSHOT STRICT=1 .

x: Interactivity, Transitions & Animations HtmlRenderer.RenderToPng / BuildDisplayList render one static snapshot of a document by themselves. To simulate mouse hover, drive CSS transition s and animation s, or read/set scroll position, a document needs an interactive DOM harness a small piece of state, bound to the document's browsing context, that tracks things a real browser would (cursor position, scroll offsets, a running clock) and feeds them back into rendering. Getting A Harness A harness needs an IRenderDevice registered on the browsing context, then is created (or retrieved, if one already exists) via GetDomHarness() : Every document not wired up this way renders exactly as before the interactive machinery is a no op until a harness exists for that browsing context. Simulating :hover Set MousePosition in viewport coordinates. The harness hit tests the layout, forces the :hover pseudo class on the topmost element under the cursor and its whole ancestor chain (matching how a real pointer makes .card:hover .title work, not just the innermost element), and raises PaintInvalidated : harness.HoveredElement exposes the currently hit tested element if you need it directly. Selecting Text Text can be selected as in a browser. A host forwards the pointer to the harness after firing mousedown , unless that was canceled: BeginTextSelection takes extend: true for a press with Shift held, and returns false when nothing can be selected there. SelectAllText() is for Ctrl+A and ClearTextSelection() removes the selection. PaintInvalidated is raised when the selection changes; showing it needs no layout, as UpdateFrame() returns the last frame with the selection painted. The selection also is the DOM's: document.GetSelection() ( getSelection() for scripts) has the members of the Selection API except modify , and its changes are painted just the same. selectstart (cancelable) and selectionchange are fired. user select is honored ( none , text , all ), what form controls show cannot be selected, and ::selection gives the colors of the highlight and the text. A host shows the cursor of text where frame.HasTextAt(x, y) is true, which does not touch the DOM. Selecting is on by default. It can be turned off for a document that has no use for it, in which case layouts do not record where their text comes from: Selecting Text Headlessly No pointer is needed to select text, e.g. to highlight search hits in a screenshot or to test what a selection covers. Select through the DOM and render; the harness only has to exist, since a document without one paints no selection: Any way of the Selection API selects: SelectAllChildren(element) , Collapse / Extend , or AddRange with a range from document.CreateRange() . RemoveAllRanges() takes the highlight away again. selection.ToString() and harness.SelectedText are the selected text as it is shown (collapsed white space, text transform , line breaks between blocks), i.e., what a browser copies to the clipboard. Without a harness, ToString() is the text of the selected nodes. Where it is comes from the range: selection.GetRangeAt(0).GetClientRects() gives a rectangle per line box, and GetBoundingClientRect() the one around them, both in viewport coordinates. The pointer gestures above work headlessly too, at coordinates of your choosing. For example, a double click selects the word under the point: Frames and Their Metrics An interactive host lays out a frame with PrepareFrame() and rasterizes it on any thread, as it no longer refers to the DOM. Every frame tells what its layout took, e.g., to show it in the developer tools of a browser: Total is the sum of the phases: Setup (web fonts and the page's default text style), Style (the render tree, i.e., matching selectors and the cascade), Layout (the boxes and what is painted), HitTesting and Subframes (the documents of iframes). x: API Documentation Configuration A browsing context needs AngleSharp.Css and a render device. WithRendering() adds the services for (its 2D context) and for data. The renderer loads the image of an it lays out (the source its render node picked for the device from srcset , sizes and the sources of a , see ElementRenderNode.ImageSource ), as AngleSharp's image element requests nothing by itself; a render waits for it, while a frame of an interactive harness paints it once it has loaded, and loads a lazy one ( loading=lazy , with scripting) only once it is within 1250px of the viewport and of the scroll containers around it. Its natural size (also naturalWidth and naturalHeight ) is divided by the density of the picked candidate (e.g. 2x ). An image not in a document (e.g. new Image() of a script) is loaded once it has a source: The render device's ViewPortWidth and ViewPortHeight are the size of the viewport, and so of the rendered image (800×600 when the context has no render device); FontSize is the default font size. Images are rendered at one device pixel per CSS pixel. Scripting Without Reflection AngleSharp.Js finds the DOM of this library by reflecting over its DOM attributes by default. A trimmed or natively compiled (AoT) application can instead hand it the registration generated for this library at build time, AngleSharp.Renderer.RendererDom.Register (a DomRegistration of AngleSharp). It declares the layout members of the library ( getBoundingClientRect , offsetWidth , ...), the observers, animations and the 2D canvas, which replace the stubs of AngleSharp.Js as they do by reflection: The registration describes the version of the library in use, so it never has to be kept in sync by hand. Several libraries are combined with DomRegistrations.Combine . Rendering A Document document.RenderToPng() renders the viewport of a document with the render device of its context: HtmlRenderer is the same with more control: it takes a render device per call, and its constructors take an IRenderBackend (default: SkiaRenderBackend ) and an ITextMeasurer (the backend, if it is one): A render shows the page at its current scroll position once the document has an interactive harness (see Interactivity), and at the top otherwise. RenderToPng is RenderToImage with the default options. Render Options RenderToImage takes RenderOptions , modeled on the screenshots of browser automation tools: Option Default Meaning FullPage false The whole page, from its top to the end of its content, instead of the viewport at its scroll position. The image is as wide as the viewport. Clip none A RenderRect of the page in CSS pixels, from the top left of the page (the scroll position plays no role). Limited to the page and the viewport's width. DeviceScaleFactor 1 Device pixels per CSS pixel, e.g. 2 for a HiDPI image. The layout stays the same; text, borders and SVG are painted sharp at the higher resolution. OmitBackground false Leaves out the white behind the page, so the image is transparent where the page paints no background. Format Png Png , Jpeg (transparent areas become white) or Webp . Quality 90 The quality of JPEG and WebP, from 0 to 100. An element renders its border box, wherever it is on the page; a Clip is then relative to the border box: A capture beyond the viewport is still laid out in the viewport: viewport units and media queries keep their values, and position: fixed boxes are painted once, at the top of the page. h: Why do web-safe fonts look the same on my machine? · Why does my text in another script show boxes? · Why does a snapshot fail when I add a new baseline? · How do I debug layout issues? · Can I render only the render tree?
x: Frequently Asked Questions Why do web safe fonts look the same on my machine? The renderer maps generic families such as serif , sans serif , and monospace to fonts bundled with it (DejaVu), not to installed fonts, so they look the same on every machine. Named families (e.g. Arial ) resolve only when installed on the host or declared via @font face ; otherwise the next entry of the font family list is used. Why does my text in another script show boxes? Characters the resolved font has no glyph for fall back to the next font family entry, then the bundled fonts (Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, Hebrew, Arabic, Devanagari), then whatever the host has installed. For other scripts (e.g. Thai or CJK) declare an @font face or install a font that covers them. Why does a snapshot fail when I add a new baseline? Visual snapshots compare the current PNG against the baseline in verification assets/ . If the baseline is missing, it is created automatically unless strict mode is enabled. How do I debug layout issues? Start with BuildDisplayList(...) and inspect the commands before rasterizing. This usually makes it easier to see whether the issue is in layout, text measurement, or final drawing. Can I render only the render tree? Yes. AngleSharp.Css exposes the render tree via window.Render(...) , which is helpful when you want to inspect computed styles before handing the document to AngleSharp.Renderer.

x: Browser Engine The BrowserEngine represents a browsing context with its history, i.e., what a single browser window (or tab) would be. It is IDisposable ; dispose it once the window goes away. Navigation Member Description NavigateAsync(address) Loads an address and adds it to the history. LoadHtmlAsync(html, address) Shows the given markup, optionally pretending it came from the given address. ReloadAsync() Loads the current address again. GoBackAsync() , GoForwardAsync() Moves through the history. GoAsync(delta) Jumps several entries back (negative) or forward. History A copy of the entries (address and title) and the index of the current one; Back and Forward list the entries before and after it, the closest first. Url , Title , IsLoading The state of the current page. CanGoBack , CanGoForward If there is something to go to. The address goes through BrowserEngine.NormalizeAddress , so what a user enters in an address bar works: example.org turns into https://example.org , while rooted paths of existing files turn into file: addresses. Addresses of the custom schemes of the engine ( BrowserOptions.SchemeHandlers ) stay as they are. Url shows where the engine is going as soon as a navigation starts, like in any browser. A failed navigation does not throw: it raises Error , is recorded in the diagnostics, and shows an error page instead. Site Information Member Description IconUrls , IconUrl Where the page's icon may come from, best first: bitmaps of , then of , /favicon.ico of an HTTP(S) page, and declared SVG icons last. IconUrl is the first of them. LoadIconAsync() Loads the first of them that is an image, with the page's cookies and cache; null if there is none. Images are recognized by their content, as servers send icons with all kinds of content types. Certificate The ServerCertificate the server of the current HTTPS page presented. GetCertificate(host) The certificate a host presented the last time the engine connected to it. A changed icon raises StateChanged . A ServerCertificate is a snapshot of what the platform verified: names, issuer, validity, fingerprints, key, the chain up to the root, and PolicyErrors ( IsValid ). The engine captures it in the validation callback of its HTTP handler, keeping the platform's verdict; a host setting its own callback (via BrowserOptions.ConfigureIo ) can use ServerCertificate.Create to the same end. A page served from the HTTP cache without a new connection may have no certificate. Threading AngleSharp is not thread safe, so all DOM work is serialized and runs on AngleSharp's event loop. This has some consequences: All Async methods of the engine may be called from any thread. They wait for the engine to be free. Code touching the DOM has to run in InvokeAsync , which also makes Document safe to use. Handlers of DOM events run on the event loop already. Engine events may be raised on any thread. A UI has to dispatch to its UI thread when handling them. Do not block the event loop (e.g., waiting for another engine operation in InvokeAsync ): it would wait for itself. Working With the DOM InvokeAsync gets the current document, which is the regular AngleSharp DOM. CSS and script integration work as in AngleSharp.Css and AngleSharp.Js: Changing the DOM invalidates the page, i.e., hosts paint a new frame on their own.
